candidate.answerReason: Equal selection chances make the boy-to-girl count ratio equal to the probability ratio, 2:3. Boys therefore constitute 2/(2+3)=2/5 of the class.

methods.label: Use proportional parts
methods.explanation:
Because each student is equally likely to be chosen, each probability equals the relevant student count divided by the total class size. Both probabilities have the same denominator, so their ratio equals the ratio of the counts.

The probability of choosing a boy is \(\frac23\) of the probability of choosing a girl. Thus the ratio of boys to girls is \(2:3\). Regard the boys as two equal parts and the girls as three equal parts. The whole class has five parts, so the requested ratio is
\[
\frac{2}{2+3}=\frac25.
\]
The answer is choice B.
